result:
I've written the five test files named in the plan. **I could not run them** — this session has no Bash/shell tool, so the "confirm they fail for the right reason" step of my instructions is unfulfilled. Everything below is static analysis, not a suite run.

## What changed

The ticket came back from Review with one complaint — the card doesn't grey — and AC-004/AC-014 were rewritten from a boolean flag to a measurable number. Those two tests are the work of this round.

**`src/features/cards/components/CardItem.test.tsx`** (rewritten)
- `AC-004` — asserts the literal `0.5` as the opacity RN resolves on `testID="card-content"`, read via `StyleSheet.flatten(...).opacity`. Before the number, it asserts the group actually *contains* the title, the amount and the type tile (`within(group)`), so a bare wrapper carrying the testID can't satisfy it while dimming nothing — that is exactly the hole the first round fell through.
- `AC-014` — the mirror: the literal `1` on the same group when the card is live. Each case is the other's control.
- Added one non-AC case pinning badge and Delete *outside* the dimmed group (the decided answer that they stay at full opacity is only enforceable that way).
- `AC-003`, `AC-008`, `AC-009` unchanged.

**`useMonobankStore.connect.test.ts`** — added `AC-013`, which had no test at all in the tree. The database singleton mock became a getter so the inherited OPES-64 cases keep their bare stand-in while this one swaps in a real throwaway database; it seeds the surviving card, reconnects the same account, and asserts one card for the account — and the *same row id*, since a destroy-and-recreate would also leave one card while orphaning the history.

**`useMonobankStore.disconnect.test.ts`** — added an explicit `OPES-68 AC-015`. It was only covered by accident: OPES-64's inherited `AC-003` in the same file happens to assert it, while that file's own `AC-015` means something else entirely. The id is ticket-prefixed for that reason, and the case carries a control (a resolving `clear()` does move the status to `idle`), because the seed is already `connected`.

**`CardStack.test.tsx`** and **`CardsRepository.test.ts`** — untouched; AC-005…AC-007 and AC-010…AC-012 were confirmed on the live build and their tests stand.

## Expected outcome, unverified

- Red: `AC-004`, `AC-014`, and the badge/Delete placement case — all three on `expect([]).toHaveLength(1)` for a `card-content` group that `CardItem.tsx` does not render yet, i.e. a failing assertion, not a collection error.
- Green at freeze: `AC-001`, `AC-002`, `AC-003`, `AC-005`–`AC-013`, `AC-015`. That is the ticket's own account of itself — only the presentation came back from Review — and per my instructions I wrote them honestly rather than manufacturing red.

No implementation file was touched; `CardItem.tsx`, `CardItem.styles.ts`, `CardStack.tsx`, `CardsRepository.ts` and `useMonobankStore.ts` are byte-unchanged.

The claim I cannot make: that these compile, collect, and fail as described. Someone needs to run `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` before this is frozen. The specific things I'd expect to bite are the `jest.Mock` variance on `mockGetClientInfo` in the connect file and whether `within(group).queryAllByText(/1\D?200\D00/)` matches the locale-formatted amount under jest's ICU.
